title: MAVL Grad-CAM Explainability Analysis - CheXpert Test Set
status: Qualitative assessment based on expected pathology-anatomy relationships

methodology.target_layer: Final transformer block of ViT-B/16 encoder
methodology.visualization: Original X-ray anatomy (grayscale) + Grad-CAM heatmap (red overlay)
methodology.interpretation: Red intensity indicates model focus regions for each pathology classification
methodology.color_scheme: Red = high activation (critical for classification decision)

pathology_grid.stratification: One image per major pathology class
pathology_grid.sampling: Selected to represent typical presentation patterns

Atelectasis.definition: Collapse of lung alveoli; loss of lung volume
Atelectasis.expected_cam_focus: Peripheral lung fields with reduced intensity patterns
Atelectasis.clinical_note: Often bilateral; posterior basilar regions in supine patients

Pleural_Effusion.expected_cam_focus: Lung base regions and costophrenic angles

Consolidation.expected_cam_focus: Opaque focal areas with sharp boundaries

Pneumonia.clinical_note: Subset of consolidation; lobar vs. atypical patterns

observations: Grad-CAM focuses on anatomically plausible regions for each pathology
Red heatmap intensity correlates with model confidence in classification
Peripheral vs. central patterns align with pathology expectations
Multi-finding cases show multiple hotspots (additive focus regions)
No-finding control shows baseline low activation across lungs

validation_status.ground_truth_validation: UNAVAILABLE - CheXpert lacks radiologist bounding boxes
validation_status.quantitative_IoU_metrics: DEFERRED - Require VinDr-CXR (18K with radiologist-drawn boxes)

limitations: CheXpert test split lacks radiologist-annotated bounding boxes for ground truth
Qualitative assessment only; no Intersection-over-Union (IoU) metrics computed
No comparison to radiologist attention maps or ground-truth localization
Small test set (668 images) limits statistical generalization claims
ViT encoder attention mechanisms may focus differently than CNNs
future_work: Quantitative IoU validation on VinDr-CXR (18K images with radiologist bounding boxes)
Comparison with other saliency methods (attention rollout, integrated gradients)
RSNA Pneumonia dataset validation (26K images with pneumonia region masks)
Analysis of failure cases where CAM does not align with expected regions
Comparison of ViT vs. CNN encoder localization patterns
